question: How can I replace a GFCI outlet in my laundry room that's been tripping constantly and won't reset?
answer: To replace a GFCI outlet, first ensure the power is off at the circuit breaker or fuse box. Remove the outlet cover plate and take a photo of the wires' layout for reference. Disconnect the black (hot) wire from the old outlet, then the white (neutral) and copper (ground) wires. Remove the old outlet and discard. Install the new GFCI outlet, ensuring the test and reset buttons are facing the correct direction. Reconnect the wires in the same order they were disconnected and replace the outlet cover plate. Test the GFCI to ensure it's working correctly.
steps: Turn off power at the circuit breaker or fuse box
Remove the outlet cover plate and take a photo of the wires' layout
Disconnect the black (hot) wire from the old outlet
Disconnect the white (neutral) and copper (ground) wires
Remove the old outlet and discard
Reconnect the wires in the same order they were disconnected
safety_info: Specific hazard: Electrical shock from live wires; Specific precaution: Ensure the power is off at the circuit breaker or fuse box before starting the repair
tips: Use a non-contact voltage tester to verify the power is off before starting the repair
Label the wires with colored tape for easier identification during reconnection
